title: Config-delta assertion oracle for structured-output sanity checks
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, config-delta driven assertion 'oracle' that runs against canary and shadow traffic to detect quality regressions specific to structured (JSON) outputs when model or serving configuration changes. This ticket scopes the first-pass implementation: per-field assertions, tolerances, and an evaluation harness that surfaces regression signals tied to a specific config diff (model version, quantization profile, prompt template, or kernel selection).

Why this is needed: existing alerts fire broadly on schema drift and token-level anomalies but do not tie regressions causally to a single change set. Teams running canary rollouts need a fast, explainable pass/fail signal per-field so rollouts can automatically stop or fall back when critical fields degrade (missing keys, type flips, out-of-range values, structured-sanity failures).

Design summary:
- Input: a config-delta (parent commit -> candidate commit) plus a fixed sample set and production-like sampling rules.
- Assertions: per-field checks: presence, type, allowed-enum, numeric range, string-length, regex, and semantic similarity buckets for free-text fields. Each assertion has a tolerance (absolute counts or percentage).
- Signal aggregation: compute per-field pass/fail and an aggregated weighted score. Emit a compact regression report that includes example failure pairs (baseline vs candidate) and the earliest commit that introduced the failure.
- Execution modes: fast canary mode (sample size ~200 per route) and thorough shadow mode (sample size configurable up to 10k).
- Integrations: console dashboard, rollout policy hooks (canary stop), and the evals pipeline for long-term trend tracking.

Acceptance criteria:
1) API to submit a config-delta and sample set and receive a detailed JSON regression report within the canary SLO (90s for 200 samples).
2) Per-field assertions implemented for presence, type, enum, numeric range, and regex.
3) Regression severity mapping: none/low/medium/high per-field and overall.
4) Console shows regression report for any canary run and rollout policy can consume the top-level pass/fail flag.
5) Unit tests covering threshold edge cases and synthetic failure injection.

Out of scope for this ticket: automatic remediation suggestions, ML-backed per-field tolerances, and cross-route causal attribution. Those are follow-ups if this proves reliable.
background: Related efforts: our structured-output regressions work has several companion tickets (schema fidelity, cohort detectors, fieldwise probes). This oracle is intended to be the fast, canary-focused gate that complements longer-running drift detectors and golden-diff comparisons. The design aims to be conservative (fail-safe) and explainable to PMs and SREs so they can act quickly during rollouts.
success_criteria:
- Canary mode returns a pass/fail + detailed per-field report in <=90s for 200 samples.
- False positive rate <5% on historical canaries (measured against labelled post-hoc regressions).
- Rollout integration exercised in at least two internal feature rollouts during the release window.
comments: 2025-02-11: Spike complete. Compared options: run-time in-process assertions vs. batch post-hoc eval. Chose post-hoc canary harness to avoid adding latency to live paths. Prototype script implemented to validate on 200-sample canaries.

2025-02-12: Decision: per-field tolerances will be explicit in config-delta manifest. Default tolerances: presence drop >5% => high, enum drift >10% => medium, type flips any => high. We will expose these in the canary UI for quick overrides.

2025-02-13: Implementation started. Basic assertion engine in Python with modular checks. Work split: Miguel implementing presence/type/enum checks, Aisha implementing numeric/range/regex and example extraction. PR for harness scaffolding created.

2025-02-15: PR review feedback from Ingrid (PM): include example pairs for top 3 failures and a short human-readable explanation for each field. Added additional metadata fields in report: sample_time, route, model_variant, quant_profile.

2025-02-17: Integration test added that injects synthetic failures (missing key, type flip) against an internal canary dataset. Observed end-to-end latency 62s for 200 samples on staging infra. Tagging runtime-1.20.

2025-02-19: Security reviewed quick checklist: no new customer PII retention; report includes hashed examples only. Confirmed with Security (ticket SEC-2381) - no full review required for MVP. Marking security_review_required=false.
2025-02-20: Ready for internal demo. Miguel to demo to SRE and PM on 2025-02-22. Next steps: hook into rollout service to allow auto-stop on 'high' severity.
